compiled_state.description:
## The failure

When an epic is decomposed into slices that land one at a time, a census run in a
single worktree sees `origin/main` plus that worktree's own commits. It does not see
sibling slices that are committed but not yet landed. Plans written from such a census
claim work that a sibling already did.

Observed in epic 87d8. Censusing slice 9's worktree made slice 8's committed-but-
unpushed substitutions invisible, so slice 10 was filed to redo work slice 8 had
already done. It was later closed as a duplicate.

The same blind spot produces a second, opposite symptom. Plan review pins material at
`origin/main`, not at worktree HEAD, so a plan written against a worktree that is
*ahead* of `origin/main` cites material the reviewer cannot see and BLOCKs. One gap,
two failure modes that look unrelated: a duplicate slice, and a review that blocks on
citations the author can see and the reviewer cannot.

## Why guidance is the fix

Nothing in the tooling can infer which branches are siblings of a slice. The author
knows. What is missing is the instruction to look, and the explanation of why a
single-worktree census is insufficient — without which the practice reads as needless
ceremony and is dropped under time pressure.

## Change

Add a census subsection to the plan-authoring guide at
`src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`, reached by `rebar explain plan`. It
must say:

- Census against the union of `origin/main` and every committed-but-unlanded sibling
  branch, not a single worktree.
- Plan review pins material at `origin/main`. A plan citing material that exists only
  on an unlanded sibling must either wait for that sibling to land, or carry an
  explicit Ordering section stating the dependency.
- Use `git grep -cF -e <term>` with fixed strings. A regex like `ticket.quality`
  matches unrelated prose such as "per-ticket quality-gate" and inflates the count.
- Sweep the whole tree per symbol rather than sampling the files you expect. Epic
  87d8's sampling census missed a reference in `docs/research/` that would have failed
  the slice's own absence criterion at the end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `rebar explain plan` output contains a census section covering all 4
      points above.
- [ ] **AC2** The section states the `origin/main` pinning rule and names both
      remedies — land the predecessor, or carry an Ordering section.
- [ ] **AC3** The section shows the fixed-string `git grep -cF` form and says why a
      regex over-matches, with a concrete over-matching example.
- [ ] **AC4** Any docs-drift or generated-artifact test covering the packaged guides
      passes against the edited guide.
- [ ] **AC5** `make verify` exits 0.

## Out of scope

Changing what plan review pins, or adding tooling to compute the sibling-branch union.
This ticket is guidance only.
compiled_state.title: Plan-authoring guide omits the sibling-branch census rule
